note: Path prefixes whose contents are claims about Logic. A change touching one of these may not use the opt-out in a pull request body, whatever its description says. Read from a file rather than held as a tuple so the merge-base ratchet can see it, and because a NEW directory that declares a LabelSet must be added here in the same change -- check-canon-citations.py refuses one that is not. A file NAMED in `exceptions` is not Logic-facing even though its path sits under one of these prefixes; see that key.
exceptions_note:
Files under a Logic-facing prefix that state no fact about Logic: they hold job names, guard names, test counts and the numbers a document may state. A change touching only these may use the `states no fact about Logic` opt-out, because there is no row of Apple's data such a change rests on and the alternative is pasting a citation that resolves and quoting its value in the diff -- manufacturing evidence, which is what the citation rule exists to stop. #937 is why: the rule made a four-line correction to GUARD-TESTS-BLIND-TO-THEIR-GUARD.json unmakeable and pushed a new ratchet file out of docs/canon for no other reason.

WHAT IS PROVED AND WHAT IS NOT. `check-canon-citations.py` rule 15 reads each file named here on every run and refuses it if it carries a `logic-canon://` reference or quotes a value the pinned corpus holds; a lookup it cannot perform is a refusal too, not a pass. That is a property of the file, re-derived every time -- which is why this list is NOT in RATCHETS: a monotonic list on top of a re-proved property adds nothing and would forbid the repair that #937 is about, the same circularity LABELSETS-WITHOUT-A-ROW.json was rescued from.

It is NOT a proof of the sentence above. A file can assert something about Logic in prose without quoting a value Apple ships -- "the dialog has three buttons" names no corpus value -- and rule 15 does not see that. Demonstrated 2026-09-20: appending such a sentence to a note here passes. So an entry is a REVIEWER'S CLASSIFICATION with a mechanical floor under it, and that is what it should be read as. Closing the gap needs these files to stop carrying free prose at all -- a closed schema per file, every field a defined identifier or a number, no `why` paragraphs -- which would mean rewriting what CI-GATE, CI-SKIPS and PROSE-NUMBERS store and what their readers expect. That is a bigger change than #937 asked for and it is the one thing that would make the claim match the check.
